questions.stem: A conservation programme breeds endangered pandas in captivity and then releases them into the wild. However, many released pandas fail to survive. What is a likely reason for this, and how might the programme be improved?

options.text: Captive-bred pandas are genetically different from wild pandas; breeding should be stopped entirely
Captive-bred pandas may lack survival skills learned in the wild (finding food, avoiding predators); the programme could include pre-release training in semi-wild environments
Pandas bred in captivity cannot reproduce in the wild
Released pandas are always rejected by wild panda populations

questions.explanation: Captive-bred animals often lack behaviours necessary for wild survival that are normally learned from parents and the environment (foraging skills, predator avoidance, social behaviours). Conservation programmes can improve success by providing pre-release training in naturalistic enclosures, ensuring suitable habitat is available, and gradually acclimatising animals before full release.

questions.stem: Sustainable development means meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs. Which of the following is the best example of sustainable development?

options.text: Clear-cutting an entire forest to build houses quickly
Fishing with no quotas to maximise short-term profits
Replanting trees at the same rate they are harvested, and using fishing quotas to allow stocks to recover
Banning all human use of natural resources

questions.explanation: Sustainable development balances human needs with environmental protection. Replanting trees at the rate of harvest ensures a continuous supply of timber without depleting forests. Fishing quotas allow fish populations to reproduce and recover, maintaining stocks for the future. Banning all resource use is not sustainable development - it ignores human needs. The goal is responsible use, not zero use.

questions.stem: Seed banks store seeds from thousands of plant species at low temperatures. Why are seed banks considered an important conservation strategy?

options.text: They allow scientists to grow new species of plants that have never existed before
They preserve the genetic diversity of plant species; if a species goes extinct in the wild, seeds can be used to reintroduce it
They provide a food supply for humans during famines
They are cheaper than protecting natural habitats

questions.explanation: Seed banks are an ex-situ (outside natural habitat) conservation strategy. They preserve the genetic diversity of plant species as an insurance policy against extinction. If wild populations are lost due to habitat destruction, disease, or climate change, stored seeds can be germinated and used for reintroduction. The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, for example, stores over a million seed samples from around the world.

questions.stem: A government creates a protected nature reserve but the reserve is surrounded by farmland with no wildlife corridors connecting it to other natural areas. Why might this reserve be less effective at conserving biodiversity than expected?

options.text: Reserves cannot protect any species from extinction
Isolated populations in the reserve cannot interbreed with other populations, reducing genetic diversity and making species more vulnerable; corridors would allow gene flow between populations
Animals prefer to live on farmland rather than in reserves
Nature reserves are too small to contain any ecosystems

questions.explanation: Isolated habitat fragments lead to small, isolated populations that suffer from reduced genetic diversity due to inbreeding. Without wildlife corridors connecting reserves, animals cannot migrate between populations to mate, so genetic diversity declines over time. This makes populations more vulnerable to disease and less able to adapt to environmental changes. Connecting reserves with corridors allows gene flow and migration.

questions.stem: Maintaining biodiversity is important not only for ecological reasons but also for human benefit. Which of the following is a practical reason why biodiversity matters to humans?

options.text: Biodiversity has no practical value to humans
Many medicines are derived from wild species; losing biodiversity means losing potential cures for diseases before they are even discovered
Biodiversity only matters in tropical countries
High biodiversity makes ecosystems less stable and productive

questions.explanation: Biodiversity has immense practical value. Many medicines come from natural compounds (e.g., aspirin from willow bark, penicillin from fungi, cancer drugs from Pacific yew trees). If species go extinct before we discover their properties, we lose potential medicines. Biodiversity also provides ecosystem services like pollination of crops, water purification, and climate regulation that humans depend on.
